content_md:
Premature ontogenic closure is the root of all prophetic evil.

The line is stolen, of course. Donald Knuth, writing in 1974 about the discipline of computer programming, warned that "premature optimization is the root of all evil" — meaning that a programmer who tunes his code before he knows where the time is actually spent will spend his effort polishing the parts that never mattered, and will have made the whole thing harder to change by the time he finds out. Measure first; commit late.
